target_customer: Trucking companies and truckers in India with no formal credit score
problem: Small truckers cannot get bank loans without a credit history; Krab built a credit profile from 200+ data points via consent APIs and offered loans from several bank partners in under 60 seconds.
business_model: Lending marketplace taking fees from bank partners, bundled with order management, invoicing, vendor payments and collections software
product_category: Fintech lending and SaaS for trucking

competitors.name: Loanzen
competitors.what: Lender to small fleet owners and driver-owners to buy trucks
competitors.traction_then: not stated in the source snippet

competitors.name: Vahak
competitors.what: Trucking marketplace aiming to enable financial transactions for truck owners
competitors.funding_then: $5M pre-Series A led by RTP Global in July 2021 (a few months after the batch)

technical_complexity.rationale: Underwriting via consent APIs and 200+ data points with several bank integrations is standard fintech engineering with some hard parts, plus the harder business problem of risk modeling thin-file borrowers.

defensibility.rationale: A credit profile built from trucking data could compound, but at founding it relied on public consent APIs and bank partners that held the credit risk and the relationship.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source describes incumbent responses to Krab specifically.

market_need_then: A 2021 India logistics source states the trucking sector is around $100B with only 30 to 40% financed by the organised sector, leaving room for lending startups.

identity.logo: Plain letter K per a profile listing

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or brand coverage found; name origin unknown and a seafood word has little connection to trucking finance.

outcome_analysis: Krab, a Winter 2021 YC company in Hyderabad, offered instant bank loans to truckers without credit scores. The YC page marks it inactive and one profile says its website became unreachable in October 2026, but no shutdown notice, stated cause or acquisition was found, so the cause is not public and no failure factor is assigned. Funding rests on aggregator data of roughly $125K to $130K, with conflicting claims of bootstrapped revenue near $1M.
notes: krab.in could not be fetched (DNS failure).
